A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOFAR work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original PointSO evaluations, simulated and real-world robot experiments, spatial VQA results, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds the semantic-orientation/chain-of-thought ablation in Table 9.

M1.justification: PointSO's encoders, additive cross-modal fusion, and cosine loss remain unchanged. SOFAR retains the same scene graph, VLM reasoning, Kabsch-Umeyama rotation calculation, and grasping/motion-planning pipeline.

E1.justification: The SpatialBot-Bench evaluation in v1 Appendix B-B and Table IX is removed. The other principal datasets, robot embodiments, and evaluation domains remain represented; the new ablation uses existing Open6DOR coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 6 removes GPT-4V from the 6-DoF SpatialBench comparison, where v1 Table IV reported its 33.9 total score. GPT-4V remains in other experiments, and comparator sets in the retained robot and EmbSpatial comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a four-condition control design independently enabling or disabling semantic orientation and chain-of-thought reasoning in Table 9. The principal benchmark protocols and training recipes remain aligned; the existing 128-object orientation split is renamed from test to validation without evidence of different samples.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a focused ablation testing whether semantic orientation contributes beyond chain-of-thought prompting. The earlier data-scaling, fusion, detection-module, corruption, cross-view, and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds error bars to the real-world success rates in Figure 7. Both versions already report three trials per task, so additional runs are not established. The new bars' statistical definition and calculation are unspecified.

E6.justification: New Table 9 reports 6-DoF overall scores of 14.2 with neither component, 13.7 with CoT only, and 45.8 with orientation only, alongside the retained 48.7 full-system result. SpatialBot-Bench results and the GPT-4V SpatialBench row disappear. Retained headline benchmark scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The semantic-orientation definition, cosine objective, scene-graph definitions, and transformation mathematics remain equivalent. No substantive formal assumption, theorem, or proof is added or removed; the omitted reference-frame discussion is conceptual exposition.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain semantic orientation, OrienText300K, PointSO/SOFAR, and the two proposed benchmarks. The rewritten abstract and introduction emphasize zero-shot and cross-embodiment generalization already claimed in v1, with the same headline performance.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix C.1 explicitly addresses attribution of gains to semantic orientation versus CoT. Conversely, v1 Section II-B's detailed conceptual connections to instance-, category-, and cross-category reference frames are omitted. Existing failure explanations and principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds direct GitHub code and HuggingFace access links to the former project-page-only header. Table 10 reports absolute training-subset sizes of 15K, 35K, 150K, and 350K where v1 Table X used percentages; this does not establish reruns. Training hyperparameters, hardware, and API-cost details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including OmniSpatial, DreamVLA, DexVLG, and Code-as-Monitor, while pruning citations such as Flamingo, PaLM-E, and RoboCat. The main positioning against existing spatial models, decoupled manipulation systems, ReKep, and Orient Anything remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively condensed and rewritten. Experiments are reordered, related work is consolidated in the appendix, and ablations receive a separate appendix section. Broader impacts and a NeurIPS checklist are added.

P2.justification: The document switches from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column NeurIPS format. v2 adds the representation-comparison Figure 2, merges the former data-construction and validation figures, trims Figure 6, adds Figure 7 error bars, and substantially relocates and resizes tables and figures.

improvement.justification: New Table 9 strengthens attribution of the manipulation results to semantic orientation by controlling for CoT. The revised exposition, resource links, and added error bars also help readers assess the work. These gains are limited by the removed SpatialBot-Bench evidence and undefined error bars; the core method and most results remain unchanged.
